properties.name: export_graph stamped a record with a replaced binary's version and said nothing, while the same server's loop_status was reporting served_by.stale: true
properties.statement:
OBSERVED 2026-09-06 at the start of a reflow2 session. The shared daemon had been started from a 0.48.0 build; the tree and the binary on disk were 0.49.0; the session-start hook said so ("the server reports its own binary as STALE") and the session discounted it because the process start time looked fresh. The first export_graph of the session wrote docs/design/reflow2.json with `stamp.reflow2_version: 0.48.0` and returned `wrote: changed` with no warning. The very next loop_status carried `served_by: {stale: true, reflow2_version: 0.48.0}` and the full STALE note. The record was restored from main and re-exported after `--stop-shared`; nothing was committed with the wrong stamp, but only because the stamp was read off the reply.

WHAT THIS IS: the mirror of fact:a-fresh-server-on-an-old-build-is-not-stale-and-stamps-confidently (2026-08-13). That one is the case the currency capability CANNOT see (a fresh server on an old build). This is the case it CAN see and DOES report — in loop_status — while the one tool whose output the staleness corrupts, export_graph, does not consult it. The information existed on the same server and did not reach the reply that mattered.

CHEAP FIX, not taken here: export_graph's reply carries the served_by block (or a one-line `stale_warning`) whenever the server's executable has been replaced since it started, so a caller reading the export result sees the stamp is from replaced code. Refusing outright is the stronger option and a design question (a stale server can still export a correct DOCUMENT; only the stamp is wrong).

BOUNDS: one instance; the export's content was correct, only its version stamp was old; the release-cut flow's own step already reads the stamp back, so a CUT would have caught it — an ordinary PR export has no such step.
